prompt:
A high-fidelity design comp of a desktop website home page. The browser viewport fills the frame edge to edge: no browser chrome, no device frame, no desk, no hands, no poster mounting.

LAYOUT, stated top to bottom. (1) A slim album-yellow header bar across the full width with a black rule beneath, ADAM WORLEY hand-lettered small at the left and four plain navigation words at the right. (2) ONE enormous full-bleed establishing illustration occupying roughly seventy percent of the page height directly beneath the header, bounded by a single even black line: a wide clear-line scene of a London riverside at midday, tower cranes and office blocks along the far bank, a bridge crossing, flat sky-blue sky with a few flat white clouds, sea-green water below. (3) Overlaid on that scene at the left, the name ADAM WORLEY hand-lettered in very large upright black capitals across two lines, with SOFTWARE ENGINEER small beneath it. (4) Below the name, an album-yellow caption box with a black outline carrying three short lines of narration text about a decade of C sharp, Terraform and Go. (5) Beneath the caption box, one adventure-red rectangular button with black outline reading GET IN TOUCH, and one paper-white outlined button beside it reading READ THE BLOG. (6) At the very bottom edge of the viewport, the top third of the next tier is just visible: three panel tops with black outlines beginning the next scene, cropped by the fold.

STYLE: ligne claire clear-line comic album artwork. One even unvarying black outline on every single shape, flat unmodulated colour fills, absolutely no gradients, no cast shadows, no shading, no texture, no photorealism, no 3D. Strict palette: sky blue, sand ochre, album yellow, paper white, sea green, steel blue, and one adventure red used only for the primary button. Headings hand-lettered in upright capitals; body text in clean small legible capitals. Composition is calm, wide, and cinematic, with generous flat colour areas.
